Gaussian mixture clustering of growth features

Source: R/pheno.R
wgh_cluster.Rd

Fits Gaussian mixture models (mclust) over a range of numbers of clusters, records BIC and ICL, and warns when the selected number sits at an edge of the search range (in the growth phenotype study (Ho 2026, medRxiv 2026.09.05.26362315) the BIC optimum first fell at the edge).

Usage

wgh_cluster(
  features,
  vars = NULL,
  G = 2:10,
  criterion = c("BIC", "ICL"),
  scale = TRUE,
  model_names = NULL
)

Arguments

features

A data frame with id and numeric feature columns (for example FPC scores joined with SITAR a, b, c).

vars

Feature columns (default: all numeric columns except id).

G

Numbers of clusters to try.

criterion

"BIC" or "ICL".

scale

Standardise features first.

model_names

Optional mclust covariance models.

Value

An object of class wgh_phenotypes with the classification, membership probabilities, BIC and ICL tables and the mclust fit.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("mclust", quietly = TRUE)) {
  feat <- aggregate(cbind(haz, baz) ~ pid, data = growdat, FUN = mean)
  names(feat)[1] <- "id"
  ph <- wgh_cluster(feat, G = 1:5)
  ph
  ph$bic
}
#> # A tibble: 70 × 3
#>    model     G   value
#>    <chr> <int>   <dbl>

#>  2 EII       2 -18509.

#>  4 EII       4 -18547.
#>  5 EII       5 -18502.
#>  6 VII       1 -18520.
#>  7 VII       2 -18492.
#>  8 VII       3 -18493.
#>  9 VII       4 -18493.
#> 10 VII       5 -18529.
